chunks: And from him, via the chain, from Hashim and Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Hashim said: 'Do not break (the seal) and do not discharge (semen).' And Ibn Bukayr said: 'Do not discharge, meaning do not come from other than this place (the designated spot).'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: These two reports are not opposed by the many reports we have previously presented, considering that they, despite being anomalous (shadh), have broken chains and are mu'rsal (disconnected).
And its ruling is that they are not contradicted by the soundly chained hadiths; and if they were safe from that, they would be construed as indicating a type of dislike (karahah).
Because although it is not forbidden (haram), it is disliked (makruh), and it is preferable to leave it in all circumstances.
That is indicated by what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking the semen seal and discharge location during intercourse in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi contextualizes these two isolated reports within the broader discourse on marital intimacy, ruling that despite their weak chains, they are not overridden by stronger narrations but rather indicate recommended dislike (karahat al-awla) rather than strict prohibition. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of balancing textual evidence with practical ease in lawful acts, emphasizing that while not forbidden, avoiding specific manners is preferable for spiritual and physical well-being.
